cards.title: One random reading tells you little
cards.body: BP changes through the day. A reading taken right after climbing stairs can alarm the whole family. Technique matters as much as the machine.

cards.title: Rest first, then measure
cards.body: Sit quietly for about five minutes before checking. No tea, smoking or exercise just before. Use the bathroom first, then stay calm and still.

cards.title: Sit properly, arm supported
cards.body: Back supported, feet flat, legs uncrossed. Rest the arm on a table so the cuff sits at heart level. No talking during the reading.

cards.title: The cuff size actually matters
cards.body: A cuff that's too small or too big gives wrong numbers. Check the size range printed on it against the upper arm. Wrap it on bare skin.

cards.title: Same time, every time
cards.body: Measure at similar times each day, like morning and evening, as your doctor suggests. Consistency makes the numbers comparable.

cards.title: Write every reading down
cards.body: Date, time, both numbers and pulse. Don't keep only the nice ones. Bring the log to the doctor, who sets the target for Papa.

cards.title: Worried by the numbers? Call, don't adjust
cards.body: Never change BP medicine based on home readings. Talk to the doctor. With chest pain, sudden weakness on one side or confusion, call 112.

takeaway: Rest first, sit right, use the right cuff, measure at the same times and log everything, then let the doctor interpret.
share: Checking BP at home? Rest 5 minutes, sit properly, right cuff size, write every reading down.
